title: Function
definition: A function is a named or addressable unit of behavior with an explicit responsibility that can be invoked through an interface.
purpose: Give behavior a boundary that can be understood, invoked, tested, and changed independently of its caller.
history: Procedures and functions are foundational program-abstraction mechanisms across programming paradigms.
mental_model: A function is a service desk: the interface states what request is accepted and what result or failure is returned, while the internal steps stay behind the desk.
analogy: A service desk; it fails if hidden shared state changes the answer without appearing in the request or contract.
common_mistakes: Treating a function as only a code container
industry_notes: A useful function boundary exposes intent and dependencies rather than merely reducing line count.
ai_notes: Require AI-generated functions to state responsibility, inputs, outputs, effects, and failure behavior.
interview_notes: Ask what makes a function boundary meaningful beyond reuse.
